messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: latency_slo_breach detected for service=redwood-inference-prod, metric=p99_decode_latency, window=5m, value=1350ms (> threshold 800ms). Pager triggered at 2026-03-15T14:02:14Z.
lee (oncall): seeing it on the dashboard, p95 up ~450ms and p99 >1.2s. Streaming stalls reported by a few customers. I'm paging eng-runtime.
maria (eng-runtime): on it, pulling logs and kernelspec events. Any recent infra or model deploys?
kevin (eng-ml): we pushed TRT8/flashattn runtime bundle to canary yesterday at 02:30 UTC, shouldn't be prod. I will double-check rollout status.
jordan (infra-sre): infra autoscale looks stable; no node OOMs, but I see increased host page faults on some GPU hosts (nvhost1-4). Kernel messages show repeated compilepath warnings after package install: "compilepath: cache miss, fallback to slow path".
frida (eng-sre): customer impact summary so far: 6 customers reported degraded streaming; 2 enterprise customers seeing tail stalls >5s and some request timeouts. No data loss.
lee (oncall): mitigation priority: reduce user impact quickly. Suggestions? rollback the kernel/compile artifacts or route traffic away from affected pool.
maria (eng-runtime): quick check: latest runtime worker image tag `runtime:v2026-03-14-trt8` spawned on subset of hosts. The compat-build enabled new compile kernels with flags `-DFLASHATN=1 -O3 -funsafe-math-optimizations` which might change floating point codegen for attention kernels. If these kernels thrash L2 or cause paging it could explain tail stalls.
kevin (eng-ml): Could force-disable FlashAttention at runtime: set env USE_FLASHATTN=0 for the inference process. That should make it use the older fused kernels.
jordan (infra-sre): I can cordon nvhost1-3 and route traffic away from them, then restart workers with env override. Cordoning will shift load to healthy pools.
lee (oncall): do it. Jordan, cordon and scale up unaffected pool. Maria, prepare a rollout with USE_FLASHATTN=0 and revert the runtime image on the affected deployment.
jordan (infra-sre): running:
```
kubectl cordon node/nvhost2
kubectl scale deployment inference-runtime --replicas=20 -n prod
kubectl set env deployment/inference-runtime USE_FLASHATTN=0 -n prod
kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-runtime -n prod
```
Cordon complete, scaling and env set. Restarting pods now.
maria (eng-runtime): watched the pods come up with USE_FLASHATTN=0. Initial metrics: p99 decode latency dropping in cordoned region, overall p95 trending down.
frida (eng-sre): confirmed on dashboards: after cordon + env flip, p99 decreased from 1.35s to ~720ms in 3 minutes. Some residual tailing but much improved.
kevin (eng-ml): note: disabling flashattn increases token cost slightly but acceptable short-term. Need a postmortem to figure out root cause: new kernel codegen, memory/workspace layout, or a compiler flag interaction causing page faults.
lee (oncall): customer comms: draft short blurb to affected customers, mention transient performance regression and mitigation steps; ask CSM to notify two enterprise customers.
frida (eng-sre): opened incident doc: https://incidents.internal/redwood/INC-2026-0315-01 (placeholder). Assigning owners: eng-runtime (maria) for root-cause, eng-ml (kevin) for kernel/attention code, infra-sre (jordan) for rollout/host fixes.
maria (eng-runtime): immediate next steps: collect heap/kvm stats on affected hosts, capture `dmesg` and kernel oops, save `/var/log/inference-runtime/*.log`, and capture sample trace for stalled request with `perf` and `nvprof` if available.
jordan (infra-sre): grabbing artifacts now:
```
ssh nvhost2 'sudo dmesg | tail -n 200' > /tmp/nvhost2-dmesg.log
sudo journalctl -u inference-worker -o short-iso --since "15 minutes ago" > /tmp/worker.log
scp artifacts to /incidents/2471122334/
```
Artifacts uploaded.
kevin (eng-ml): reproduced locally by running model with `runtime:v2026-03-14-trt8` + flashattn enabled on a large batch; I see elevated page-faults and occasional kernel fallback to scalar attention (explainable by compilepath fallback logs). Sharing snippet:
```
[warn] compilepath: attempt optimized kernel failed, falling back to generic_attention() at 0x7f...
[info] attention_kernel: workspace exceeded L2 threshold, paging to device memory
```
This points to working set growth in new kernels.
maria (eng-runtime): hypothesis: new kernel variant uses bigger temporary buffers that push working set beyond on-GPU L2 or reserved pinned memory, increasing host-device page activity under certain sequence lengths. That leads to stalls at tail under streaming with many concurrent small requests (prefix KV churn).
lee (oncall): mitigation status -> stable. Rolling back runtime image on affected ASG to `runtime:v2026-03-12` for full rollback while we investigate. Jordan proceeding with rollback command.
jordan (infra-sre): rollback issued: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/inference-runtime -n prod --to-revision=42` on the affected ASG. Monitoring.
frida (eng-sre): monitoring shows p99 now ~610ms cluster-wide. We'll keep the incident page updated. Postmortem owners: Maria/Kevin/Jordan. Follow-ups: build a regression test for working set growth across sequence lengths, add kernel-level telemetry for temp buffer sizes, and gate canary promotions on page-fault metrics.
lee (oncall): thanks all. I'll hand off to oncall-next at 14:30 UTC with summary: kernel/compilepath regression from TRT8/FlashAttention bundle caused increased GPU page faults and tail latency; mitigations: cordon affected hosts, disable flashattn, rollback runtime image; customers partially impacted, no data loss.
maria (eng-runtime): will collect final traces and start root-cause debugging.
kevin (eng-ml): will reproduce with matrix of seq-len x batch-size and submit fix/patch to attention kernel to reduce temporary allocation or fallback to cached KV placement.
jordan (infra-sre): will add node-level pagefault alert to catch regressions earlier.
frida (eng-sre): closing notes: create postmortem, schedule RCA session 48h after incident, and update runbook with a quick mitigation checklist (env toggle, cordon, rollback).
lee (oncall): handing off to next oncall: take it from here, watch for regressions on canary promotions. :thumbsup:
